`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- Copilot independently flagged the same `LockCodeManagerError`-swallowed-at-DEBUG issue that my review agents surfaced — that's strong signal it's a real concern, not just one tool nitpicking.
- The update listener and options flow are computing essentially the same diff with different shapes — the listener wants axis-separated `{slots,locks}_to_{add,remove}`, the options flow wants cartesian `pairs_added`. A single helper can produce both.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

## Copilot's two new comments (commit `6739372`)

**1. [`config_flow.py:191-195`](https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/pull/983#discussion_r3093602327) — `LockCodeManagerError` swallowed at DEBUG**

Real issue. `_async_get_all_codes` catches *all* `LockCodeManagerError` at debug level, so genuine `LockDisconnected`/communication failures are indistinguishable from the three "expected skip" cases (missing entity, unsupported platform, missing config entry). My own review agents independently flagged this. Suggested fix: distinguish expected-skip (a dedicated sentinel exception or a returned `None`) from real provider failures, and log real failures at WARNING.

**2. [`config_flow.py:486`](https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/pull/983#discussion_r3093602392) — YAML form default uses entire `user_input` dict**

Real (pre-existing) bug, easy fix: `default=user_input` → `default=user_input.get(CONF_SLOTS, {})`. The current code prefills the slots selector with the whole submitted dict on validation-error re-render. Trivial and we're already touching this code, so worth folding in.

## Reuse opportunities

You're right that the config flow class has gotten dense. The places I see worth consolidating:

### A. Diff calculation (your example) — strongest case for reuse

`__init__.py:async_update_listener` computes `slots_to_add/remove`, `locks_to_add/remove` from `data` vs `options`. `config_flow.py:_maybe_confirm_then_persist` computes `added_pairs` from old vs new entry data. Same underlying inputs, slightly different views.

A tiny helper in `data.py` could produce all three views in one shot:

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class EntryConfigDiff:
    slots_added: dict[int, Any]
    slots_removed: dict[int, Any]
    locks_added: list[str]
    locks_removed: list[str]
    pairs_added: set[tuple[str, int]]   # only the options flow uses this today
    pairs_removed: set[tuple[str, int]]

def compute_entry_config_diff(old, new) -> EntryConfigDiff: ...
```

Update listener consumes the slot/lock axes; options flow consumes `pairs_added`. One source of truth, one place to test the int/str slot-key normalization.

### B. The two "persist after clear" methods

```python
# config flow
async def _create_entry_and_clear_slots(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
    await self._clear_all_pending_slots()
    return self.async_create_entry(title=self.title, data=self.data)

# options flow
async def _persist_options_and_clear_slots(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
    await self._clear_all_pending_slots()
    return self.async_create_entry(title="", data=self._pending_options)
```

Identical structure. Could collapse to one mixin method that captures `(title, data)` at the same time `_next_step` is assigned — e.g. `self._set_persist_target("", user_input)` paired with `self._next_step = self._clear_then_persist`. Removes `_pending_options` as a separate piece of state.

### C. The scoped_codes builder

The 6-line block that filters `all_codes` to only `added_pairs` is the kind of thing that reads better as a named function:

```python
scoped_codes, scoped_instances = _scope_codes_to_pairs(
    all_codes, lock_instances, added_pairs
)
```

Small win, but it makes `_maybe_confirm_then_persist` read top-to-bottom as: *"compute diff → query → scope → check → confirm or persist"*.

### D. The `LockCodeManagerError` issue (Copilot #1)

Worth noting that fixing this could become its own helper too: `_async_check_existing_usercodes` could be split into two concerns — a "should we even try?" check (raises `LockCodeManagerError` for the three skip cases) and the actual `async_internal_get_usercodes()` call (whose errors propagate as real failures). This is the cleanest way to give the caller the signal needed.

---

**My recommendation for a follow-up PR (not this one):** A and D are the highest-leverage. B and C are nice-to-haves that fit naturally if we're already in there.

For *this* PR, I'd suggest the minimal-touch fix for both Copilot comments:
- Fix #2 (YAML default) — trivial one-liner
- Fix #1 (LockCodeManagerError) — small split of `_async_check_existing_usercodes` into "skip checks" (raises) and "do the call" (propagates real errors)

**Want me to:**
1. Make the two Copilot fixes in this PR, then
2. Open a follow-up PR (or queue a TODO) for the bigger A/B/C reuse refactor?

Or do you want all of it in this PR?

170	    ent_reg: er.EntityRegistry,
171	    lock_entity_ids: list[str],
172	) -> tuple[dict[str, dict[int, str | SlotCode]], dict[str, Any]]:
173	    """Query locks for all usercodes.
174	
175	    Returns a tuple of:
176	    - Dict keyed by lock entity ID, each value being a dict of slot number to
177	      code value (including SlotCode.EMPTY for empty slots). Callers must
178	      filter as needed.
179	    - Dict keyed by lock entity ID to temporary lock provider instances, for
180	      reuse in clearing slots.
181	    """
182	    result: dict[str, dict[int, str | SlotCode]] = {}
183	    lock_instances: dict[str, Any] = {}
184	    # Query sequentially to avoid flooding networks (e.g. Z-Wave, Matter)
185	    # with simultaneous requests across multiple locks
186	    for lock_entity_id in lock_entity_ids:
187	        try:
188	            lock_instance, usercodes = await _async_check_existing_usercodes(
189	                hass, dev_reg, ent_reg, lock_entity_id
190	            )

196	            )
197	        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
198	            _LOGGER.warning(

200	                lock_entity_id,
201	                exc_info=True,
202	            )
203	        else:
204	            if usercodes:
205	                result[lock_entity_id] = usercodes
206	                lock_instances[lock_entity_id] = lock_instance
207	    return result, lock_instances

This is distinct from\n    ``LockCodeManagerError`` (raised by providers for real failures like\n    ``LockDisconnected``) so the caller can log skips at DEBUG and real\n    failures at WARNING.\n    \"\"\"\n\n\ndef _async_build_lock_instance(\n    hass: HomeAssistant,\n    dev_reg: dr.DeviceRegistry,\n    ent_reg: er.EntityRegistry,\n    lock_entity_id: str,\n) -> Any:\n    \"\"\"Build a temporary lock provider instance for ``lock_entity_id``.\n\n    Performs setup-time checks (entity in registry, supported platform,\n    parent config entry exists) and instantiates the provider class.\n\n    Raises ``_LockQuerySkipped`` if any setup-time check fails. The provider\n    constructor itself is not wrapped — failures there propagate as\n    unexpected exceptions and are caught one level up.\n    \"\"\"\n    lock_entry = ent_reg.async_get(lock_entity_id)\n    if not lock_entry:\n        _LOGGER.warning(\n            \"Entity %s not found in registry; skipping usercode check\",\n            lock_entity_id,\n        )\n        raise _LockQuerySkipped(lock_entity_id)\n    if lock_entry.platform not in INTEGRATIONS_CLASS_MAP:\n        _LOGGER.debug(\n            \"Lock %s uses unsupported platform %s; skipping usercode check\",\n            lock_entity_id,\n            lock_entry.platform,\n        )\n        raise _LockQuerySkipped(lock_entity_id)\n    lock_config_entry = hass.config_entries.async_get_entry(lock_entry.config_entry_id)\n    if lock_config_entry is None:\n        _LOGGER.warning(\n            \"Config entry for lock %s not found; skipping usercode check\",\n            lock_entity_id,\n        )\n        raise _LockQuerySkipped(lock_entity_id)\n\n    return INTEGRATIONS_CLASS_MAP[lock_entry.platform](\n        hass, dev_reg, ent_reg, lock_config_entry, lock_entry\n    )\n\n\nasync def _async_get_all_codes(\n    hass: HomeAssistant,\n    dev_reg: dr.DeviceRegistry,\n    ent_reg: er.EntityRegistry,\n    lock_entity_ids: list[str],\n) -> tuple[dict[str, dict[int, str | SlotCode]], dict[str, Any]]:\n    \"\"\"Query locks for all usercodes.\n\n    Returns a tuple of:\n    - Dict keyed by lock entity ID, each value being a dict of slot number to\n      code value (including SlotCode.EMPTY for empty slots). Callers must\n      filter as needed.\n    - Dict keyed by lock entity ID to temporary lock provider instances, for\n      reuse in clearing slots.\n\n    Locks are skipped (with logging) for three failure modes:\n    - Setup-time skip (entity missing, unsupported platform, etc.) → DEBUG\n    - Provider failure (e.g. ``LockDisconnected``) → WARNING with details\n    - Unexpected exception → WARNING with traceback\n    \"\"\"\n    result: dict[str, dict[int, str | SlotCode]] = {}\n    lock_instances: dict[str, Any] = {}\n    # Query sequentially to avoid flooding networks (e.g. Z-Wave, Matter)\n    # with simultaneous requests across multiple locks\n    for lock_entity_id in lock_entity_ids:\n        try:\n            lock_instance = _async_build_lock_instance(\n                hass, dev_reg, ent_reg, lock_entity_id\n            )\n        except _LockQuerySkipped:\n            # Already logged by _async_build_lock_instance with the\n            # appropriate level for the specific skip reason\n            continue\n\n        try:\n            usercodes = await lock_instance.async_internal_get_usercodes()\n        except LockCodeManagerError as err:\n            # Real provider failure (e.g. LockDisconnected) — surface it\n            # so users can see why a lock's codes weren't checked\n            _LOGGER.warning(\n                \"Failed to get usercodes from %s: %s\",\n                lock_entity_id,\n                err,\n            )\n            continue\n        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001\n            _LOGGER.warning(\n                \"Failed to get usercodes from %s; this lock's codes will not be shown\",\n                lock_entity_id,\n                exc_info=True,\n            )\n            continue\n\n        if usercodes:\n            result[lock_entity_id] = usercodes\n            lock_instances[lock_entity_id] = lock_instance\n    return result, lock_instances"
}

# TODO

## User-Facing Features

- **Config flow: lock reset in options flow** — Extend the lock reset step
  (clear/adopt unmanaged codes) to the options flow when new locks are added.
  Adopt should merge into existing slot config (preserve names, settings) rather
  than creating fresh entries. Key considerations: (1) compute "unmanaged" against
  the *new* slot config being submitted, not the current stored config, so removing
  a slot doesn't immediately offer to clear it; (2) existing managed slots on
  write-only locks (Matter) show as UNKNOWN — filter these out using the new config
  rather than offering to reset them; (3) if re-setting managed PINs for safety
  after lock reset, note this to the user.
- **Config flow: conflicting integration detection** — Warn if Keymaster or other
  code management integrations are detected at setup.
- **Clear all unmanaged codes** — Button or service to clear unmanaged code slots
  on a lock.
- **Bulk operations** — Enable/disable multiple slots at once.
- **Import/export slot configuration**
- **PIN validation** — Warn on simple PINs ("1234", "0000"), duplicate PINs
  across slots, format violations against lock requirements, and slot conflicts
  across config entries.
- **Service actions:**
  - `set_temporary_code` — time-limited PIN
  - `generate_pin` — auto-generate secure PIN
  - `bulk_enable` / `bulk_disable`
- **Custom Jinja templates** — Ship `.jinja` macros for LCM entity resolution
  (e.g. `lcm_slot_entities(config_entry_id, slot_num)`). Auto-install to
  `custom_templates/` during setup.
- **Drift detection alerting** — Alert users when drift detection consistently
  fails (e.g. lock offline). Currently only logged.

## Providers

**Current:** Akuvox, Matter, Schlage, Z-Wave JS, Virtual (testing)

**Open PRs:** ZHA (#739), MQTT/Zigbee2MQTT (#740)

**Future:** Nuki, SwitchBot, SmartThings

**Cannot support:** esphome (no API), august/yale/yalexs_ble/yale_smart_alarm
(library limitations)

  optimistic pushes from set/clear methods and relying solely on events. The

44	## Architecture Considerations
45	
46	- **Event-driven vs optimistic push updates** — For providers that support push
47	  events (Matter LockUserChange, Z-Wave value updates), consider removing
48	  optimistic pushes from set/clear methods and relying solely on events. The
49	  event is the lock's actual confirmation the credential was stored, while
50	  optimistic pushes only confirm the service call was accepted. Event-only
51	  updates give a single source of truth and simpler code, at the cost of a
52	  brief latency window before the coordinator updates. Z-Wave may still need
53	  optimistic pushes to avoid sync loops with stale cache reads.
54	
55	- **Matter provider: direct Matter client commands** — Replace HA service calls
56	  (`matter.set_lock_credential`, etc.) with direct `MatterClient.send_device_command()`
57	  calls to get structured response objects (e.g., `SetCredentialResponse.status`
58	  with `DlStatus.kDuplicate`). Currently duplicate detection relies on string
59	  matching the error message. Direct commands would give typed status codes for
60	  duplicate, occupied, resource exhausted, etc.
61	
62	## Code Quality
63	
64	- **Dual storage pattern** — Simplify `data` + `options` config entry pattern.
65	  Document when to use each.
66	- **Coordinator-owned sync managers** — Move sync manager lifecycle from binary
67	  sensor entities to coordinator (survives entity recreation during config
68	  updates).
69	- **Dataclass conversion** — Convert config entry data and internal dicts to typed
70	  dataclasses with `from_dict`/`from_entry` class methods.
71	- **Websocket optimization** — Add optional `include_entities`/`include_locks`
72	  flags to `get_config_entry_data` command.
73	- **Entity registry change detection** — Warn if LCM entity IDs change (reload
74	  required).
75	- **Provider diagnostics** — Add `get_diagnostic_data()` to `BaseLock` for
76	  provider-specific diagnostic information.
77

> AGENT

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- **The exception split is the higher-value fix** — it changes observable behavior (logs go from DEBUG to WARNING for actionable failures), which means a user whose Z-Wave lock is offline during setup will now see a useful warning instead of a silent skip. Tests had to be expanded with `caplog.at_level("WARNING")` because the old test's `RuntimeError` path doesn't exercise the new `LockCodeManagerError`-specific branch.
- **Splitting into a sentinel exception (`_LockQuerySkipped`)** rather than reusing `LockCodeManagerError` for both purposes is the right call — it makes the contract explicit at the type level rather than relying on "we know this function only raises LCMError for skip cases" tribal knowledge. The provider-raised LCMError now has a dedicated catch arm and a meaningful log message.
- **Provider constructor failures** still propagate as `Exception` (not `_LockQuerySkipped`), preserving the prior commit's "treat as unexpected" semantics — which is intentional, since a constructor failure means the provider class itself is broken, not that the lock is unsupported.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

## Summary

Three commits pushed to `feat/lock-reset-step`:

**`d9f0516` — Address Copilot review:**
- Split `_async_check_existing_usercodes` into:
  - `_async_build_lock_instance` (sync, raises `_LockQuerySkipped` for the 3 setup-time skip cases)
  - The actual provider call now lives in `_async_get_all_codes` with a dedicated `LockCodeManagerError` catch arm at WARNING level
- Three failure modes now distinct: skip → DEBUG, provider failure → WARNING with `lock_id: error`, unexpected → WARNING + traceback
- Fixed YAML form default: `default=user_input` → `default=user_input.get(CONF_SLOTS, {})`
- New test `test_async_get_all_codes_provider_failure_logs_warning` asserts the WARNING signal
- 31 tests, 100% coverage, ruff clean

**`7fd4340` — TODO bookkeeping:**
- Removed the now-completed "lock reset in options flow" item
- Queued the bigger reuse refactor (A + B + C from my earlier plan):
  - `compute_entry_config_diff(old, new)` shared by the update listener + options flow
  - Collapse `_create_entry_and_clear_slots` / `_persist_options_and_clear_slots` into one mixin helper
  - Extract `scoped_codes` builder

The follow-up refactor is sized for its own PR — sharing a helper between `config_flow.py` and `__init__.py:async_update_listener` will touch the listener's diff-and-act logic and warrants its own focused review.

- Subclassing `LockCodeManagerError` makes `_LockQuerySkipped` a member of the project's exception family, so any future generic `except LockCodeManagerError` handler (e.g. in coordinator or repair logic) will catch it without surprise.
- The structural separation — `_LockQuerySkipped` raised only by the sync setup-time check, `LockCodeManagerError` raised only by the async provider call — means even with the inheritance, the two catch arms never compete. They live in different try blocks.

> AGENT

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- **The current two-try-block structure is a workaround for not having `LockCodeManagerProviderError`** — once the parent exists, we can collapse them into one try with three `except` arms. That's the strongest concrete win, not just typing nicety.
- **An exception hierarchy refactor is a cross-cutting change** — it touches every provider and every catch site. Worth its own PR even though the diff would be modest, because reviewers should be able to evaluate "did we correctly classify each existing exception" without it being mixed into a feature.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

Yes — strong yes, separate PR. Concrete benefits:

## Why it's worthwhile

1. **It collapses the workaround we just put in.** Today's `_async_get_all_codes` has two try blocks specifically because we couldn't say "catch only real provider failures, not setup-time skips". With a `LockCodeManagerProviderError` parent, we'd have:

   ```python
   try:
       lock_instance = _async_build_lock_instance(...)
       usercodes = await lock_instance.async_internal_get_usercodes()
   except _LockQuerySkipped:
       # DEBUG: setup-time skip
   except LockCodeManagerProviderError as err:
       # WARNING: real provider failure
   except Exception:
       # WARNING with traceback: unexpected
   ```

   One try, three semantically distinct catches.

2. **It gives downstream code (coordinator, repair flows, sync managers) a clean question to ask.** "Did this error originate from the lock provider?" is a frequent thing to want to know — currently you can't ask it without inspecting the type list.

## Suggested classification

```
LockCodeManagerError
├── _LockQuerySkipped                  # internal, config-flow only
├── EntityNotFoundError                # LCM internal — entity registry miss
└── LockCodeManagerProviderError       # NEW: anything originating from a provider
    ├── LockDisconnected               # comms failure
    ├── CodeRejectedError              # lock rejected the call
    │   └── DuplicateCodeError
    └── ProviderNotImplementedError    # provider said "I don't do this"
```

The split I'd draw: `EntityNotFoundError` stays at the LCM-base level because it's about LCM's view of the entity registry, not lock behavior. The other four are all things the provider did/told us.

## Why separate PR

- Cross-cutting (touches every provider's exception raising and the catch sites in coordinator/sync/repair)
- Mechanically simple but conceptually load-bearing — reviewers should evaluate the classification carefully, not have it slipped in alongside a feature
- This PR is already at 7 commits with 264 stmts of changed flow code; merging it cleanly without entangling more concerns is the right call

122	class _LockQuerySkipped(LockCodeManagerError):
123	    """Raised when a lock should be skipped before any provider call.
124	
125	    Used internally by ``_async_build_lock_instance`` to signal one of the
126	    three expected setup-time skip conditions (missing entity, unsupported
127	    platform, missing config entry). Subclasses ``LockCodeManagerError`` so
128	    it belongs to the project's exception family, but is caught separately
129	    from provider-raised ``LockCodeManagerError`` (e.g. ``LockDisconnected``)
130	    so setup-time skips log at DEBUG and real provider failures log at
131	    WARNING.
132	    """
133	
134	
135	def _async_build_lock_instance(
136	    hass: HomeAssistant,
137	    dev_reg: dr.DeviceRegistry,
138	    ent_reg: er.EntityRegistry,
139	    lock_entity_id: str,
140	) -> Any:
141	    """Build a temporary lock provider instance for ``lock_entity_id``.
142	
143	    Performs setup-time checks (entity in registry, supported platform,
144	    parent config entry exists) and instantiates the provider class.
145	
146	    Raises ``_LockQuerySkipped`` if any setup-time check fails. The provider
147	    constructor itself is not wrapped — failures there propagate as
148	    unexpected exceptions and are caught one level up.
149	    """
150	    lock_entry = ent_reg.async_get(lock_entity_id)
151	    if not lock_entry:
152	        _LOGGER.warning(
153	            "Entity %s not found in registry; skipping usercode check",
154	            lock_entity_id,
155	        )
156	        raise _LockQuerySkipped(lock_entity_id)
157	    if lock_entry.platform not in INTEGRATIONS_CLASS_MAP:
158	        _LOGGER.debug(
159	            "Lock %s uses unsupported platform %s; skipping usercode check",
160	            lock_entity_id,
161	            lock_entry.platform,
162	        )
163	        raise _LockQuerySkipped(lock_entity_id)
164	    lock_config_entry = hass.config_entries.async_get_entry(lock_entry.config_entry_id)
165	    if lock_config_entry is None:
166	        _LOGGER.warning(
167	            "Config entry for lock %s not found; skipping usercode check",
168	            lock_entity_id,
169	        )
170	        raise _LockQuerySkipped(lock_entity_id)
171	
172	    return INTEGRATIONS_CLASS_MAP[lock_entry.platform](
173	        hass, dev_reg, ent_reg, lock_config_entry, lock_entry
174	    )
175	
176	
177	async def _async_get_all_codes(
178	    hass: HomeAssistant,
179	    dev_reg: dr.DeviceRegistry,
180	    ent_reg: er.EntityRegistry,
181	    lock_entity_ids: list[str],
182	) -> tuple[dict[str, dict[int, str | SlotCode]], dict[str, Any]]:
183	    """Query locks for all usercodes.
184	
185	    Returns a tuple of:
186	    - Dict keyed by lock entity ID, each value being a dict of slot number to
187	      code value (including SlotCode.EMPTY for empty slots). Callers must
188	      filter as needed.
189	    - Dict keyed by lock entity ID to temporary lock provider instances, for
190	      reuse in clearing slots.
191	
192	    Locks are skipped (with logging) for three failure modes:
193	    - Setup-time skip (entity missing, unsupported platform, etc.) → DEBUG
194	    - Provider failure (e.g. ``LockDisconnected``) → WARNING with details
195	    - Unexpected exception → WARNING with traceback
196	    """
197	    result: dict[str, dict[int, str | SlotCode]] = {}
198	    lock_instances: dict[str, Any] = {}
199	    # Query sequentially to avoid flooding networks (e.g. Z-Wave, Matter)
200	    # with simultaneous requests across multiple locks
201	    for lock_entity_id in lock_entity_ids:
202	        try:
203	            lock_instance = _async_build_lock_instance(
204	                hass, dev_reg, ent_reg, lock_entity_id
205	            )
206	        except _LockQuerySkipped:
207	            # Already logged by _async_build_lock_instance with the
208	            # appropriate level for the specific skip reason
209	            continue
210	
211	        try:
212	            usercodes = await lock_instance.async_internal_get_usercodes()
213	        except LockCodeManagerError as err:
214	            # Real provider failure (e.g. LockDisconnected) — surface it
215	            # so users can see why a lock's codes weren't checked
216	            _LOGGER.warning(
217	                "Failed to get usercodes from %s: %s",
218	                lock_entity_id,
219	                err,
220	            )
221	            continue
222	        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
223	            _LOGGER.warning(
224	                "Failed to get usercodes from %s; this lock's codes will not be shown",
225	                lock_entity_id,
226	                exc_info=True,
227	            )
228	            continue
229	
230	        if usercodes:
231	            result[lock_entity_id] = usercodes
```

  "command": "gh pr create --title \"Add LockCodeManagerProviderError parent for provider-raised exceptions\" --body \"$(cat <<'EOF'\n## Proposed change\n\nIntroduces an intermediate exception class `LockCodeManagerProviderError` so callers can distinguish \"the lock provider raised this\" from other `LockCodeManagerError` subclasses without enumerating every type.\n\n### New hierarchy\n\n```\nHomeAssistantError\n└── LockCodeManagerError\n    ├── _LockQuerySkipped              (config-flow internal sentinel)\n    ├── EntityNotFoundError            (LCM internal — registry miss)\n    └── LockCodeManagerProviderError   (NEW)\n        ├── LockDisconnected\n        ├── CodeRejectedError\n        │   └── DuplicateCodeError\n        └── ProviderNotImplementedError (also NotImplementedError)\n```\n\n`EntityNotFoundError` stays at the LCM-base level because it's about LCM's view of the entity registry, not lock behavior. The four provider-raised errors all originate from the `BaseLock` subclass talking to its hardware/service layer, so they share the new parent.\n\n### Why\n\nConcretely, this lets `_async_get_all_codes` (added in #983) collapse its two-try workaround into a single try with three semantically distinct except arms:\n\n- `_LockQuerySkipped` → DEBUG (expected setup-time skip)\n- `LockCodeManagerProviderError` → WARNING with error message\n- `Exception` → WARNING with traceback\n\nThe two try blocks existed because we couldn't say \"catch only real provider failures, not setup-time skips\" — both raised `LockCodeManagerError`. With the new parent, that distinction is in the type system.\n\n### Compatibility\n\nExisting catch sites all continue to work because the hierarchy widens, never narrows:\n\n- [`coordinator.py`](https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/blob/main/custom_components/lock_code_manager/coordinator.py): catches `LockCodeManagerError` (still catches everything)\n- [`sync.py`](https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/blob/main/custom_components/lock_code_manager/sync.py): catches `CodeRejectedError`, `LockDisconnected` directly (still works — those types are unchanged)\n- [`providers/_base.py`](https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/blob/main/custom_components/lock_code_manager/providers/_base.py): catches `ProviderNotImplementedError` directly (still works)\n\nNo catch site needed updating.\n\n## Type of change\n\n- [x] Code quality improvements to existing code or addition of tests\n\n## Additional information\n\n- 570 tests pass, 100% coverage on `config_flow.py`, 97% on `exceptions.py`\n- Updated inheritance assertions for `LockDisconnected`, `CodeRejectedError`, `DuplicateCodeError`, `ProviderNotImplementedError`\n- Added explicit test that `EntityNotFoundError` is **not** a `LockCodeManagerProviderError` (locks in the classification)\nEOF\n)\" 2>&1 | tail -3",

> AGENT

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- **Cooperative MRO worked silently**: `ProviderNotImplementedError(LockCodeManagerProviderError, NotImplementedError)` — Python figures out the linearization without us doing anything special. Because `LockCodeManagerProviderError` already inherits from `LockCodeManagerError` → `HomeAssistantError`, and `NotImplementedError` is a built-in Exception, the MRO is clean.
- **The "hierarchy widens, never narrows" invariant** is what made this a no-touch change for callers. If we'd renamed `LockCodeManagerError` → `LockCodeManagerProviderError` (collapsed instead of split), every `except LockCodeManagerError` site would have been a behavior change. The intermediate-class approach is non-breaking by construction.
- **The collapsed try in `_async_get_all_codes`** is one line shorter and far more readable — three `except` arms with three log levels reads top-to-bottom as the actual policy ("skip / surface / panic"), where the previous version split that same policy across two unrelated `try` blocks.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

PR #1026 created: https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/pull/1026

**Summary**

`exceptions.py` (+15, -3): introduced `LockCodeManagerProviderError` between `LockCodeManagerError` and the four provider-raised exceptions (`LockDisconnected`, `CodeRejectedError`/`DuplicateCodeError`, `ProviderNotImplementedError`).

`config_flow.py` (+5, -11): collapsed `_async_get_all_codes`'s two-try workaround into one try with three distinct `except` arms.

`tests/test_exceptions.py` (+22, -7): updated inheritance assertions; added negative test that `EntityNotFoundError` is not a provider error.

`tests/test_config_flow.py` (+5, -8): swapped the test's mock to raise `LockDisconnected` (more representative of real provider behavior).

`TODO.md`: removed the now-completed entry.

570 tests pass, lint clean.

Once #1026 merges, the splits PR (the diff helper + persist consolidation) is next.

> AGENT

Pushed `2c13546` to PR #1026.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- **The dual approach (migrate + defensive catch)** trades off "purity" for safety. Migrating alone would be cleaner, but a third-party provider could still raise the bare base — and for that user, a confusing traceback is worse than a clean warning. The defensive arm costs ~10 lines and makes the failure mode self-evident in code.
- **The redundant `except (LockDisconnected, LockCodeManagerError)` arms in matter/schlage are a fossil** of the previous flat hierarchy — once `LockDisconnected` IS-A `LockCodeManagerError` you only ever needed the broader catch. The new `LockCodeManagerProviderError` is the "right grain" for these availability checks: catch any provider-originated failure, treat as unavailable.
- **Tests with `pytest.raises(LockCodeManagerError, match=...)` survived the migration unchanged** — that's the LSP-style benefit of widening (subclass → still matches base). Reading the existing tests gave me confidence the migration was safe before I started touching providers.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

  "old_string": "def build_slot_unique_id(",
  "new_string": "@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)\nclass EntryConfigDiff:\n    \"\"\"Diff between two LCM entry configurations.\n\n    Produced by :func:`compute_entry_config_diff`. Provides three views of\n    the same diff so callers can ask the question that fits their need:\n\n    - **By axis** (slot dict + lock list): used by the update listener,\n      which adds/removes slot entities and lock providers along independent\n      axes.\n    - **By unchanged set**: ``slots_unchanged`` enumerates slot numbers\n      present in both configs, used by the listener to reconcile per-slot\n      configuration changes.\n    - **By cartesian pair**: ``pairs_added`` / ``pairs_removed`` give\n      ``(lock, slot)`` tuples that are new or gone, which the options flow\n      uses to detect existing-codes hazards on newly-added pairs (catches\n      both \"new slot on existing lock\" and \"new lock with existing slot\").\n    \"\"\"\n\n    slots_added: dict[int, Any]\n    slots_removed: dict[int, Any]\n    slots_unchanged: set[int]\n    locks_added: list[str]\n    locks_removed: list[str]\n    pairs_added: frozenset[tuple[str, int]]\n    pairs_removed: frozenset[tuple[str, int]]\n\n    @property\n    def has_changes(self) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"True if any slot or lock was added or removed.\"\"\"\n        return bool(\n            self.slots_added\n            or self.slots_removed\n            or self.locks_added\n            or self.locks_removed\n        )\n\n\ndef compute_entry_config_diff(\n    old: Mapping[str, Any], new: Mapping[str, Any]\n) -> EntryConfigDiff:\n    \"\"\"Compute the diff between two LCM entry config mappings.\n\n    Each input is a mapping with ``CONF_LOCKS`` (list[str]) and\n    ``CONF_SLOTS`` (dict[int|str, dict]) keys. Slot keys are normalized\n    to ``int`` so callers can rely on ``int`` comparisons regardless of\n    where the dict was loaded from (HA storage round-trips them as ``str``).\n    \"\"\"\n    old_slots: dict[int, Any] = {\n        int(k): v for k, v in old.get(CONF_SLOTS, {}).items()\n    }\n    new_slots: dict[int, Any] = {\n        int(k): v for k, v in new.get(CONF_SLOTS, {}).items()\n    }\n    old_locks: list[str] = list(old.get(CONF_LOCKS, []))\n    new_locks: list[str] = list(new.get(CONF_LOCKS, []))\n\n    old_lock_set = set(old_locks)\n    new_lock_set = set(new_locks)\n    old_pairs: set[tuple[str, int]] = {\n        (lock, slot) for lock in old_locks for slot in old_slots\n    }\n    new_pairs: set[tuple[str, int]] = {\n        (lock, slot) for lock in new_locks for slot in new_slots\n    }\n\n    return EntryConfigDiff(\n        slots_added={k: v for k, v in new_slots.items() if k not in old_slots},\n        slots_removed={k: v for k, v in old_slots.items() if k not in new_slots},\n        slots_unchanged=set(old_slots) & set(new_slots),\n        locks_added=[lock for lock in new_locks if lock not in old_lock_set],\n        locks_removed=[lock for lock in old_locks if lock not in new_lock_set],\n        pairs_added=frozenset(new_pairs - old_pairs),\n        pairs_removed=frozenset(old_pairs - new_pairs),\n    )\n\n\ndef build_slot_unique_id("
}

  "old_string": "class _ExistingCodesFlowMixin:",
  "new_string": "def _scope_codes_to_pairs(\n    all_codes: dict[str, dict[int, str | SlotCode]],\n    lock_instances: dict[str, Any],\n    pairs: Iterable[tuple[str, int]],\n) -> tuple[dict[str, dict[int, str | SlotCode]], dict[str, Any]]:\n    \"\"\"Filter raw query results to only the ``(lock, slot)`` pairs given.\n\n    Used by the options flow so the mixin's clearing logic cannot touch\n    already-managed ``(lock, slot)`` pairs even though they appear in the\n    raw query result. The mixin's ``_clear_existing_slot`` only iterates\n    pairs present in ``_all_codes``, so scoping there constrains the blast\n    radius without the mixin needing to know about pairs.\n    \"\"\"\n    scoped_codes: dict[str, dict[int, str | SlotCode]] = {}\n    for lock, slot in pairs:\n        if (code := all_codes.get(lock, {}).get(slot)) is not None:\n            scoped_codes.setdefault(lock, {})[slot] = code\n    scoped_instances = {lock: lock_instances[lock] for lock in scoped_codes}\n    return scoped_codes, scoped_instances\n\n\nclass _ExistingCodesFlowMixin:"
}

> AGENT

Found the root cause: `get_slot_data` does `slots_dict.get(slot_num)`. The listener's local `new_slots` previously preserved str keys from storage, but the diff helper now produces int keys downstream — entities created with int `slot_num` can't look up their data in the str-keyed stored dict. Normalizing the listener's locals to int makes everything consistent:

> TOOL

tool_use Edit
id: toolu_01Q9M4fPxc6Dets39vHetiMx
```json
{
  "replace_all": false,
  "file_path": "/Users/raman/projects/lock_code_manager/custom_components/lock_code_manager/__init__.py",
  "old_string": "    curr_slots: dict[int, Any] = {**config_entry.data.get(CONF_SLOTS, {})}\n    new_slots: dict[int, Any] = {**config_entry.options.get(CONF_SLOTS, {})}\n    new_locks: list[str] = [*config_entry.options.get(CONF_LOCKS, [])]",
  "new_string": "    # Normalize slot keys to int. HA's JSON storage round-trips them as\n    # str; downstream code (entities, get_slot_data) treats them as int.\n    # Keeping the listener's locals consistent with diff.slots_added/etc.\n    # — which the diff helper int-normalizes — means a slot_num passed to\n    # an entity's __init__ matches the key under which its data is stored.\n    curr_slots: dict[int, Any] = {\n        int(k): v for k, v in config_entry.data.get(CONF_SLOTS, {}).items()\n    }\n    new_slots: dict[int, Any] = {\n        int(k): v for k, v in config_entry.options.get(CONF_SLOTS, {}).items()\n    }\n    new_locks: list[str] = [*config_entry.options.get(CONF_LOCKS, [])]"
}

> AGENT

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- **The slot-key debugging detour was the most valuable lesson**: the original `compute_entry_config_diff` aggressively normalized keys to int — which broke the listener's invariant that downstream code (entities → `get_slot_data`) gets the same key type that the storage uses. The fix ("normalize for comparisons, preserve for outputs") is the right design for any helper that produces *both* derived values (set diffs) AND passes through original data (the slot config dicts). The inline comment in `helpers.py:191` (`slot if slot in data[CONF_SLOTS] else str(slot)`) was the smoking gun — somebody had hit this same str/int mismatch before.
- **`functools.partial` for `_next_step`** beats lambda by being explicit about intent ("this method, with these args bound") and beats stored state attributes by keeping the bound values in the closure (no extra `_pending_*` instance var to remember to clear).
- **Frozen dataclass with multiple "views" of the same diff** is a pattern worth knowing: each consumer asks the question that fits its model (axis vs. cartesian) without forcing one to translate. The slight duplication in storage is the price of keeping consumer code idiomatic.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

PR #1028 created: https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/pull/1028

**Summary:**

`data.py` (+97): new `EntryConfigDiff` frozen dataclass + `compute_entry_config_diff()` helper.

`__init__.py` (-3): listener uses `diff.slots_added/removed`, `diff.locks_added/removed`, `diff.slots_unchanged`, `diff.has_changes`. Removed unused `curr_locks` local.

`config_flow.py` (+55, -45): added `_clear_then_create_entry(title, data)` mixin method, removed `_create_entry_and_clear_slots` / `_persist_options_and_clear_slots` / `_pending_options`. New module helper `_scope_codes_to_pairs()`. Options flow `_maybe_confirm_then_persist` rewritten on top of the diff helper — net shorter and clearer.

`tests/test_data.py` (+138): 9 new tests covering the diff helper, including the str/int key-mixing case that caused the initial test failures and the cross-axis "new lock with existing slot" case.

580 tests pass, lint clean. Ready for review.

> AGENT

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- **Set math is a tempting metaphor that doesn't quite fit here.** The natural operation `config1 - config2` is "subset of config1 not in config2" — but the consumers want different views (slots-axis, locks-axis, pair-cartesian, unchanged-set). Squashing those into one return shape forces translation at every call site.
- **`EntryConfig` as a typed container is a separately good idea**, just orthogonal to the diff API. The hard problem it would solve (str/int key inconsistency at the storage boundary) is bigger than this PR.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

Honest take: **good instinct, but the operator-overloading flavor is the wrong half to apply here.** Let me split the idea:

## Two separable proposals inside your question

### A. `EntryConfig` as a typed container (genuinely valuable)

Right now we pass `dict[str, Any]` around with `CONF_LOCKS`/`CONF_SLOTS` magic keys. An `EntryConfig` would:

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class EntryConfig:
    locks: list[str]
    slots: dict[int, dict[str, Any]]  # always int keys

    @classmethod
    def from_entry(cls, entry: ConfigEntry) -> EntryConfig: ...
    @classmethod
    def from_mapping(cls, m: Mapping) -> EntryConfig: ...
    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]: ...
```

Real wins:
- **Centralizes the str/int slot-key normalization at one boundary** (the smoking gun in `helpers.py:191` and the bug we just hit)
- Replaces `[CONF_SLOTS]` magic-string indexing with `.slots` attribute access
- IDE/pyright actually understands what's in there

### B. Set-math operators on `EntryConfig` (this is where I'd push back)

The natural domain for set math is the cartesian `(lock, slot)` pair set. But `config1 - config2` would have to return... what? An `EntryConfig`? With which locks and slots?

The listener actively wants AXIS-SEPARATED views:
- "slots being added" (regardless of which lock)
- "locks being added" (regardless of which slot)  
- "slots unchanged" so it can reconcile per-slot config changes

A `__sub__` returning an `EntryConfig` of "what's in lhs but not rhs" can't represent those without forcing the listener to re-derive them. We'd be moving complexity from the helper into every consumer.

The reconcile loop is the clearest example. It needs:
```python
for slot_num in unchanged:
    reconcile(old.slots[slot_num], new.slots[slot_num])
```
That's "the slots present in both, with both versions accessible". Set algebra on configs gives you ONE side's view, not both.

## What I'd recommend

**For this PR**: keep `compute_entry_config_diff(old, new) -> EntryConfigDiff` as-is. The function name is honest about what it does (a multi-axis diff), and the dataclass output is a passive container of derived views.

**As a follow-up PR**: introduce `EntryConfig` purely as a typed boundary container. Migrate `get_slot_data`, `get_managed_slots`, the listener's reads, and the options flow's reads to consume `EntryConfig`. That PR would:

1. Centralize the str→int slot key normalization at `EntryConfig.from_entry()` — single fix for the longstanding inconsistency
2. Naturally absorb `compute_entry_config_diff(old: EntryConfig, new: EntryConfig)` — same shape, just typed inputs
3. Touch many read sites, so it deserves its own focused review

That's the highest-leverage version of your idea: the typed container, without forcing set-math semantics that don't fit the actual question.

1. Add a TODO entry for "Centralize entry config in EntryConfig dataclass"
2. Or just keep this PR scoped and we revisit if/when the str/int issue bites again?

## PR #1028 Summary

**Intent**: Reduce code duplication across the config flow, options flow, and update listener by extracting shared diff logic and consolidating slot-clearing logic.

**Key Changes**:

1. **`compute_entry_config_diff()` helper** (`data.py`, +97 lines): A frozen dataclass `EntryConfigDiff` providing three views of the same diff:
   - By-axis: `slots_added`/`slots_removed`/`locks_added`/`locks_removed` for the listener
   - Unchanged set: `slots_unchanged` for per-slot reconciliation
   - Cartesian pairs: `pairs_added`/`pairs_removed` for detecting existing-codes hazards on newly-added (lock, slot) pairs
   - Smart key-type normalization: internally treats `"1"` and `1` as the same slot for set comparisons, but preserves the new mapping's key type in outputs (critical for listener indexing back into source dicts)

2. **Mixin consolidation**: Replaced `_create_entry_and_clear_slots()` and `_persist_options_and_clear_slots()` with a single `_clear_then_create_entry(title, data)` method. Both flows now bind via `functools.partial` when a confirmation step exists, or call directly when not.

3. **Module helper `_scope_codes_to_pairs()`**: Extracts the 5-line scoping logic used by options flow to filter query results to only newly-added pairs, preventing the clearing logic from touching already-managed pairs.

**Files Modified**:
- `__init__.py`: Uses the new diff helper in `async_update_listener`; replaces manual slot/lock change detection
- `config_flow.py`: Uses `_clear_then_create_entry` and `_scope_codes_to_pairs`; removes `_pending_options` state
- `data.py`: New `EntryConfigDiff` and `compute_entry_config_diff()`
- `tests/test_data.py`: 9 new tests covering diff edge cases (str/int key mixing, cartesian pair detection)

**Notable Architectural Decision**: Slot dicts preserve the *new* mapping's key type to match the listener's indexing convention—this avoids subtle bugs where a str-keyed slot from JSON storage wouldn't match int-keyed voluptuous output.

**Coverage**: 580 tests pass, 100% on `config_flow.py`, new helper fully tested. Listener and options flow behavior unchanged.

Here are the real bugs I found in this diff:

---

**1. `_scope_codes_to_pairs` silently drops lock instances when a lock has no codes**

`config_flow.py`, lines ~263-271 (`_scope_codes_to_pairs`)

```python
scoped_instances = {lock: lock_instances[lock] for lock in scoped_codes}
```

`scoped_codes` only contains locks for which at least one code was found (`is not None`). If a lock in `pairs` exists in `lock_instances` but has no non-None codes for any of the requested slots, it's absent from `scoped_codes` and thus absent from `scoped_instances`. This is intentional by design — but the bug is the inverse: `lock_instances[lock]` will raise `KeyError` if a lock in `scoped_codes` was not returned by `_async_get_all_codes` (e.g., provider error, lock not reachable). The caller passes `locks_to_query` which are derived from `diff.pairs_added`, but `_async_get_all_codes` could return a subset. There is no guard against the lock being missing from `lock_instances`, so this would crash with `KeyError` instead of failing gracefully.

---

**2. `partial` captures mutable `self.data` dict by reference, not by value**

`config_flow.py`, lines ~543-548 (`async_step_yaml`)

```python
self._next_step = partial(
    self._clear_then_create_entry,
    title=self.title,
    data=self.data,
)
```

`self.data` is a mutable dict. The `partial` captures the reference to the dict object, not a snapshot. If any code between this assignment and the eventual call to `_next_step` (via `async_step_existing_codes_confirm`) mutates `self.data`, the entry will be created with the mutated data. In the yaml flow this is lower risk, but it's a latent correctness issue — the previous `_create_entry_and_clear_slots` used `self.data` at call time, which was fine, but `partial` with a mutable default introduces an implicit shared-state dependency. A `data=dict(self.data)` or `data={**self.data}` shallow copy would eliminate this.

---

**3. `slots_unchanged` in `EntryConfigDiff` uses the *new* mapping's key type, but `__init__.py` uses it to index into both `new_slots` and `old_slots`**

`__init__.py`, lines ~875-882; `data.py`, lines ~113-115

The diff comment in `data.py` says "Preserve the new mapping's key type — the listener's reconcile loop indexes back into `raw_new_slots` / `raw_old_slots` and needs the original key type." But when the update listener calls `_async_reconcile_slot_entities`, it passes `slot_num` from `diff.slots_unchanged`, which uses `new`'s key type. If `new` is `options` (which may be `int`-keyed after voluptuous validation) but `data` (which is `str`-keyed from JSON storage) is also consulted inside `_async_reconcile_slot_entities`, lookups with `int` keys into a `str`-keyed dict will silently miss. This is exactly the str/int confusion this PR is trying to fix — the fix is only partial if the reconcile function indexes into `curr_slots` (old, `str`-keyed) using a key derived from `diff.slots_unchanged` (new, `int`-keyed).

This is the most subtle real bug: `slots_unchanged` deliberately preserves the `new` key type, but the loop at `__init__.py:875` presumably passes that key into code that also needs to look up the old slot config, and there's no normalization there.

---

**4. `compute_entry_config_diff` called with `old_data` built from `get_entry_data` results directly in `config_flow.py`**

`config_flow.py`, lines ~697-702

```python
old_data = {
    CONF_LOCKS: get_entry_data(self.config_entry, CONF_LOCKS, []),
    CONF_SLOTS: get_entry_data(self.config_entry, CONF_SLOTS, {}),
}
diff = compute_entry_config_diff(old_data, user_input)
```

`get_entry_data` returns the value directly from `config_entry.data` or `config_entry.options` (a merged view). The returned dict for `CONF_SLOTS` is the live object from the config entry — not a copy. `compute_entry_config_diff` then does `list(old.get(CONF_LOCKS, []))` and set operations over it, which is read-only and safe. However, `old_data` is constructed with the live reference, meaning if `get_entry_data` for `CONF_SLOTS` returns an object shared with the entry's internal state, and if anything else were to mutate it during an async yield inside `compute_entry_config_diff` (there are none currently, it's sync), this would be a hazard. This is lower severity — it's currently safe because `compute_entry_config_diff` is synchronous and does no mutation — but worth noting as a fragility.

---

**Summary of real bugs by severity:**

| # | Severity | File | Issue |
|---|----------|------|-------|
| 3 | High | `data.py` + `__init__.py` | `slots_unchanged` uses new-key-type but reconcile also accesses old (str-keyed) dict |
| 1 | Medium | `config_flow.py` | `KeyError` if lock present in pairs but absent from `lock_instances` result |
| 2 | Low | `config_flow.py` | `partial` captures mutable `self.data` ref, not snapshot |
| 4 | Low | `config_flow.py` | Live config entry object passed into diff without copy (currently safe, fragile) |

## PR #1028 Code Review — Issues Found

### Issue 1 — Imperative loop in `_scope_codes_to_pairs` instead of comprehension

**File:** `custom_components/lock_code_manager/config_flow.py` — `_scope_codes_to_pairs` function (around lines 247–266 in the diff)

```python
scoped_codes: dict[str, dict[int, str | SlotCode]] = {}
for lock, slot in pairs:
    if (code := all_codes.get(lock, {}).get(slot)) is not None:
        scoped_codes.setdefault(lock, {})[slot] = code
scoped_instances = {lock: lock_instances[lock] for lock in scoped_codes}
```

**Guidance violated:** AGENTS.md — *"Prefer comprehensions over loops, `next()` over for/break, concise idiomatic expressions"*; and the `feedback_idiomatic_python.md` memory — *"list/dict/set comprehensions over loops."*

The `scoped_codes` body is a grouping loop with `setdefault`/mutation. While a grouping comprehension is slightly less natural than a flat one, the project guidance explicitly prefers comprehension-style. A canonical idiomatic form uses `itertools.groupby` or a nested dict comprehension. At minimum, the code could be structured as:

```python
# group pairs by lock
from itertools import groupby
scoped_codes = {
    lock: {slot: all_codes[lock][slot] for slot in slots if all_codes.get(lock, {}).get(slot) is not None}
    for lock, slots in groupby(sorted(pairs), key=lambda p: p[0])
    if lock in all_codes
}
```

The imperative loop-with-mutation pattern is the exact form the project feedback asks to avoid.

---

### Issue 2 — `_scope_codes_to_pairs` docstring is not Google style

**File:** `custom_components/lock_code_manager/config_flow.py` — `_scope_codes_to_pairs` docstring

```python
    """Filter raw query results to only the ``(lock, slot)`` pairs given.

    Used by the options flow so the mixin's clearing logic cannot touch
    already-managed ``(lock, slot)`` pairs even though they appear in the
    raw query result. The mixin's ``_clear_existing_slot`` only iterates
    pairs present in ``_all_codes``, so scoping there constrains the blast
    radius without the mixin needing to know about pairs.
    """
```

**Guidance violated:** AGENTS.md — *"Docstrings: Google style, required for all public functions."*

Google-style docstrings require `Args:` and `Returns:` sections for public functions with parameters and return values. This function has three parameters and a return tuple; the docstring omits both sections. All other new public additions in this PR (`compute_entry_config_diff`, `EntryConfigDiff` class, `has_changes`, `_clear_then_create_entry`) have the same omission. Among these, `compute_entry_config_diff` (public, in `data.py`) and `_scope_codes_to_pairs` (module-level in `config_flow.py`) are the most visible violators since they have non-trivial parameters.

---

### Issue 3 — `_next_step` assignment contract is untyped and unsafe by design

**File:** `custom_components/lock_code_manager/config_flow.py` — `_ExistingCodesFlowMixin`

The mixin's docstring (not changed here, but the PR's `_clear_then_create_entry` explicitly relies on `_next_step`) describes `_next_step` as "the coroutine to run after the user confirms clearing." The PR assigns `_next_step` like this:

```python
self._next_step = partial(
    self._clear_then_create_entry,
    title=self.title,
    data=self.data,
)
```

`_clear_then_create_entry` has required keyword-only arguments (`title`, `data`). If a future subclass author assigns `self._next_step = self._clear_then_create_entry` without `partial`, the mixin will call `_next_step()` with no arguments and get a `TypeError` at runtime. There is no type annotation on `_next_step` (it is not declared in `__init__` or as a class variable with a `Callable` type), so the type checker cannot catch this misuse.

**Guidance violated:** AGENTS.md — *"Type annotations: Keep older style (`dict[str, Any]` not `dict[str, Any] | None` where possible)"* — this implies type annotations are expected. More directly, this is a substantive API safety issue that the project's own convention (typed attributes on mixins) is meant to prevent.

The fix is to declare `_next_step: Callable[[], Awaitable[dict[str, Any]]]` in the mixin's state and make `_clear_then_create_entry`'s required args explicit in the type, or restructure so `_next_step` is always a zero-arg callable (the `partial` approach already does this, but it needs a type declaration).

---

### Issue 4 — Tests in `test_data.py` do not require `hass` but the `_slot()` helper uses a bare `dict` return type annotation

**File:** `tests/test_data.py`, line 14

```

**Guidance violated:** AGENTS.md — *"Type annotations: Keep older style (`dict[str, Any]` ...)"* — the return type is `dict` (bare), not `dict[str, Any]`. This is a minor but concrete violation of the project's annotation convention. All other typed helpers in this codebase use `dict[str, Any]`.

This is the only real annotation issue. The tests themselves do not manipulate `hass.data` manually — they are pure unit tests of a pure function, which is completely appropriate given `compute_entry_config_diff` takes no `hass` argument. The test structure is correct.

Here are the top findings from cross-referencing past review comments with PR #1028's diff.

---

**Finding 1 — `slots_removed` docstring claims wrong key-type guarantee**
**File:** `custom_components/lock_code_manager/data.py`, line 83 (in PR #1028)
**Active Copilot comment on this PR.**

The class docstring states that `slots_added`, `slots_removed`, and `slots_unchanged` all "preserve the *new* mapping's key type." That is only true for `slots_added` and `slots_unchanged`. `slots_removed` is built from `raw_old_slots.items()`, so its keys follow the *old* mapping's key type. When `old` is str-keyed JSON storage and `new` is int-keyed voluptuous output, callers treating `slots_removed` keys as new-mapping-typed will get the wrong type. The docstring needs to be fixed to say `slots_removed` preserves the *old* key type, or the implementation needs to normalize the keys.

---

**Finding 2 — `slots_unchanged` key type mismatch can cause `KeyError` in the update listener**
**File:** `custom_components/lock_code_manager/__init__.py`, lines 878–887 (in PR #1028)
**Flagged by Copilot as a suppressed low-confidence comment in the PR #1028 review.**

`slots_unchanged` is built from `raw_new_slots` keys (new-mapping key type, typically `int` from voluptuous). But `curr_slots` is `config_entry.data.get(CONF_SLOTS, {})`, which comes from JSON storage and is therefore `str`-keyed. The reconcile loop does:

```python
for slot_num in diff.slots_unchanged:
    await _async_reconcile_slot_entities(
        config_entry, slot_num,
        curr_slots[slot_num],   # KeyError if curr_slots is str-keyed and slot_num is int
        new_slots[slot_num],
        ...
    )
```

If `curr_slots` has str keys (e.g., `"1"`) and `slot_num` is `int` (e.g., `1`), `curr_slots[slot_num]` raises `KeyError`. This is exactly the type-mixing scenario the PR explicitly documents as a known hazard. The fix from PR #983 and the helper itself both normalize for comparison but not for the final lookup.

---

**Finding 3 — `EntryConfigDiff` is frozen but holds mutable containers, misleading immutability claim**
**File:** `custom_components/lock_code_manager/data.py`, line 92; `tests/test_data.py`, line 145 (in PR #1028)
**Active Copilot comment on this PR; also a pattern raised in PR #989.**

`EntryConfigDiff` is `frozen=True` (attribute *reassignment* is blocked) but `slots_added`, `slots_removed`, and `slots_unchanged` are plain `dict`, `dict`, and `set`. The docstring says "supports use as cached state" and `test_diff_is_immutable` asserts "immutability." Both claims are misleading — `diff.slots_added[1] = {}` and `diff.slots_unchanged.add(99)` work fine. The fix is either to use `types.MappingProxyType` for the dicts and `frozenset` for `slots_unchanged`, or to remove the immutability language from both the docstring and the test.

---

**Finding 4 — `_clear_then_create_entry` docstring retains a stale implementation note about `functools.partial`**
**File:** `custom_components/lock_code_manager/config_flow.py`, lines 333–356 (in PR #1028)
**Pattern: stale docstring guidance; related to several past Copilot comments in PRs #983 and #1006 about misleading inline documentation.**

The `_clear_then_create_entry` method docstring says "Bind `title`/`data` via `functools.partial` when assigning `_next_step`, or call directly when no confirmation step is required." This is advice about *how callers use the method*, not how the method itself works — and it becomes inaccurate if a future caller uses a lambda or a different mechanism. More directly, the sentence "Clearing happens BEFORE `async_create_entry()` because `async_create_entry()` only builds a FlowResult dict — the entry isn't persisted until after this step returns" is a repeat of the comment Copilot flagged in PR #983 as incorrect: clearing before `async_create_entry()` is the right order precisely *because* the entry is not yet persisted, so "Clearing happens BEFORE" is fine, but the explanation of *why* it matters is still there even after the PR #983 comment pointed out that approach isn't ideal (codes are cleared before the config entry is successfully written). The safer pattern would be to clear after triggering entry creation, e.g., as a fire-and-forget task.

---

**Finding 5 — `_async_get_all_codes` silent-failure pattern is still present for non-`LockCodeManagerError` exceptions**
**File:** `custom_components/lock_code_manager/config_flow.py`, lines ~230–250 (in PR #1028; code not changed by PR #1028 but context matters)
**Previously flagged in PR #983**: "silently suppress actionable failures and make 'no codes detected' indistinguishable from 'lock unreachable'."

PR #1028 does not touch `_async_get_all_codes`, and a broad `except Exception` path logs at `WARNING` without re-raising. PR #983's Copilot comment called for a dedicated exception for expected skip conditions so real failures could be surfaced differently. That recommendation was partially addressed (there is now a `_LockQuerySkipped` exception type and `LockCodeManagerProviderError` is handled separately), but the bare `LockCodeManagerError` catch and the broad `Exception` catch both `continue` without any UI feedback to the user that a lock could not be queried — the options flow will silently skip that lock's codes. This is the same silent-failure concern that has been raised across PRs #983 and #1026.

Here is the review of PR #1028 (commit cc50c49).

## Summary

The PR extracts a `compute_entry_config_diff` helper into `data.py` and rewires both `async_update_listener` and `_maybe_confirm_then_persist` to use it, eliminating two independent reimplementations of the same logic. It also lifts `_clear_then_create_entry` up into `_ExistingCodesFlowMixin` (replacing the now-deleted per-flow `_create_entry_and_clear_slots` / `_persist_options_and_clear_slots` methods).

---

## Issues Found

### 1. `slots_unchanged` key type mismatch breaks `curr_slots[slot_num]` lookup

**File:** `custom_components/lock_code_manager/__init__.py`, lines 878–886
**Docstring at odds:** `data.py` line 79: *"preserve the new mapping's key type"* / comment at line 143–145: *"the listener's reconcile loop indexes back into raw_new_slots / raw_old_slots and needs the original key type to find the slot config dict."*

The docstring *correctly* explains the intent — `slots_unchanged` preserves the **new** mapping's key type. At the listener call site, `new_slots` and `curr_slots` are built from:

```python
curr_slots: dict[int, Any] = {**config_entry.data.get(CONF_SLOTS, {})}
new_slots: dict[int, Any] = {**config_entry.options.get(CONF_SLOTS, {})}
```

Both `config_entry.data` and `config_entry.options` are loaded from Home Assistant's JSON storage, so their slot keys are **strings**. The type annotation says `dict[int, Any]` but that's aspirational — the actual runtime keys are `str`.

`compute_entry_config_diff` is called as `compute_entry_config_diff(config_entry.data, config_entry.options)`. Both sides come from JSON storage, so both have `str` keys. `slots_unchanged` will therefore contain **`str`** keys (preserving `new`'s type, as documented).

The reconcile loop then does:

```python
for slot_num in diff.slots_unchanged:          # slot_num is str, e.g. "1"
    await _async_reconcile_slot_entities(
        ...,
        curr_slots[slot_num],   # KeyError if curr_slots is str-keyed *and* so is slot_num — OK
        new_slots[slot_num],    # same
```

In the storage→storage case (both str-keyed) this *works* by accident because both the `curr_slots` dict and the `slots_unchanged` keys are `str`. **But** the original code before this PR used `set(curr_slots).intersection(new_slots)` — which also worked because it intersected the actual key sets without type normalization.

The real risk surfaces in a mixed-type scenario: if for any reason `config_entry.data` has `int` keys (e.g., just after a fresh options-flow write that put `int`-keyed voluptuous output into `data`), `curr_slots` will have `int` keys, but `slots_unchanged` preserves the **new** (`options`) type. If `options` is `str`-keyed (loaded from disk on the next HA restart), `curr_slots["1"]` would hit a `KeyError` on an `int`-keyed dict.

The docstring at line 143 says the listener *needs the original key type to find the slot config dict*, but it can only guarantee that for the `new_slots` lookup. The `curr_slots[slot_num]` lookup at line 882 is implicitly assuming `curr_slots` has the same key type as the new mapping — there is no `int(slot_num)` normalization there as there was for the set intersection in the old code. **This is a latent bug when `data` and `options` come from different origins with different key types.**

A safe fix: `curr_slots[slot_num]` → `curr_slots.get(slot_num, curr_slots.get(int(slot_num), {}))`, or normalize both `curr_slots` and `new_slots` to `int`-keyed dicts at the top of the listener (which the type annotations already claim they are).

---

### 2. `_scope_codes_to_pairs` – `lock_instances[lock]` can `KeyError` when a lock queried successfully has no codes

**File:** `custom_components/lock_code_manager/config_flow.py`, line 265

```python
scoped_instances = {lock: lock_instances[lock] for lock in scoped_codes}
```

`lock_instances` is populated by `_async_get_all_codes` only when `usercodes` is truthy (line 243–244):

```python
if usercodes:
    result[lock_entity_id] = usercodes
    lock_instances[lock_entity_id] = lock_instance
```

So if a lock returns an empty usercodes dict, it is absent from both `result` (i.e., `all_codes`) and `lock_instances`. The `_scope_codes_to_pairs` loop then filters `all_codes.get(lock, {}).get(slot)` — if the lock isn't in `all_codes` it produces no entry in `scoped_codes`, so `scoped_codes` won't contain that lock either. This means the `lock_instances[lock]` lookup only fires for locks already present in `all_codes`, and since `all_codes` and `lock_instances` are co-populated, the `KeyError` path cannot actually be reached in practice.

However, the docstring for `_scope_codes_to_pairs` does not mention this implicit precondition ("callers must pass `lock_instances` and `all_codes` from the same `_async_get_all_codes` call"). If someone ever passes a partially-populated `lock_instances` dict, line 265 will raise. Minor robustness issue, not a current bug.

---

### 3. `_clear_then_create_entry` docstring vs. `async_step_ui` / `async_step_code_slot` call path — `_next_step` is NOT `_clear_then_create_entry` in the UI path

**File:** `custom_components/lock_code_manager/config_flow.py`, lines 336–353 (docstring) and lines 458–460

The docstring says:

> *"Bind `title`/`data` via `functools.partial` when assigning `_next_step`, or call directly when no confirmation step is required."*

In `async_step_ui` (lines 458–460), when there are slots to clear:

```python
self._next_step = self.async_step_code_slot
return await self.async_step_existing_codes_confirm()
```

`_next_step` is set to `async_step_code_slot`, not to `_clear_then_create_entry`. Then, when the user works through all slots in `async_step_code_slot` and the last slot is submitted, it calls `_clear_then_create_entry` **directly** (line 510–512). This means:

- The user confirms clearing → `async_step_existing_codes_clear` calls `self._next_step()` → `async_step_code_slot()` → user fills slots → last slot triggers `_clear_then_create_entry` directly.

This path is **functionally correct** — clearing happens before `async_create_entry`. But the docstring's framing implies `_next_step` should always point to `_clear_then_create_entry` (possibly via `partial`). The `async_step_ui` case violates that expectation by using `_next_step` as a "continue to next step" pointer rather than a "finalize" pointer. Not a bug, but the docstring is misleading about the invariant — it says "assign `_next_step`… when assigning `_next_step`" and implies it always points to `_clear_then_create_entry`, when in practice the UI path chains through `async_step_code_slot` first.

---

### 4. Listener `no-options` guard — still correct

**File:** `custom_components/lock_code_manager/__init__.py`, lines 744–747

```python
# No need to update if there are no options because that only happens at the end
# of this function
if not config_entry.options:
    return
```

The comment says "that only happens at the end of this function" — referring to `async_update_entry(..., options={})` at line 893. `compute_entry_config_diff` is now called **after** this guard (line 784), so the early-return still correctly prevents a redundant call triggered by the `options={}` write at the end. This invariant is **preserved**.

---

### 5. `_ExistingCodesFlowMixin.__init__` contract — still upheld

The docstring says *"Inheriting flow must call `_init_existing_codes_state()` from its `__init__`."* Both `LockCodeManagerFlowHandler.__init__` (line 397) and `LockCodeManagerOptionsFlow.__init__` (line 626) do so. The deletion of `self._pending_options` from `LockCodeManagerOptionsFlow.__init__` is correct — the ivar was only used by the deleted `_persist_options_and_clear_slots` method. Contract upheld.

---

### 6. `_scope_codes_to_pairs` "cannot touch already-managed pairs" claim — upheld

The function correctly restricts `scoped_codes` to only the slots from `pairs`, so `_clear_existing_slot`, which iterates `self._all_codes`, can only see and clear those scoped-in slots. The invariant is correctly implemented.

---

## Summary Table

| # | Severity | Claim violated | Location |
|---|----------|---------------|----------|
| 1 | **Bug (latent)** | `slots_unchanged` preserves new key type, but `curr_slots[slot_num]` at reconcile assumes same type; fails when `data` is int-keyed and `options` is str-keyed | `__init__.py` L878–882 |
| 2 | Minor robustness | `lock_instances[lock]` has implicit precondition not stated in docstring | `config_flow.py` L265 |
| 3 | Doc mismatch | `_clear_then_create_entry` docstring implies `_next_step` always points to it; UI path sets `_next_step = async_step_code_slot` | `config_flow.py` L336–353 vs L459 |
| 4–6 | No issue | Listener guard, mixin init contract, scoping invariant all upheld | — |

Based on a thorough investigation of the diff, git history, and all the code paths specifically called out in the review request, here is the finding:

---

**No bugs were introduced by PR #1028.**

Here is the detailed analysis for each concern:

**1. Slot key str/int consistency**

`compute_entry_config_diff` correctly handles the str/int mismatch. It int-normalizes both sides for set comparisons (`old_int_keys`, `new_int_keys`) and preserves the *new* mapping's key type in the slot-dict outputs. In the listener, both `config_entry.data` and `config_entry.options` come from HA's JSON storage, so both are str-keyed — the slots_unchanged/slots_added/slots_removed outputs carry str keys, and the `curr_slots[slot_num]`/`new_slots[slot_num]` lookups at lines 882–883 use the same str keys. The removal UID matching (`f"{slot_num}|"` prefix in `callbacks.py:232`) is also safe because `f"{1}|key" == f"{'1'}|key"` in Python's f-string formatting.

**2. `_async_setup_new_locks` — `new_slots` key type**

The `new_slots` variable at line 826 is still `{**config_entry.options.get(CONF_SLOTS, {})}` (str-keyed from JSON), exactly as before. `diff.slots_added` is not passed here — `new_slots` is passed unchanged. No regression.

**3. Data→options migration round-trip**

The migration at lines 416–419 sets `data={}` and `options={**config_entry.data}`, triggering the listener with `config_entry.data = {}`. `compute_entry_config_diff({}, options)` produces `old_int_keys = set()`, so all slots appear in `slots_added` and `slots_unchanged` is empty. This is identical to the pre-PR behavior where `curr_slots = {}` made every slot appear in `slots_to_add`.

**4. `_maybe_confirm_then_persist` — removal of explicit `int()` casts**

The old explicit `int(slot)` casts in the old pair-set construction are replaced by `old_int_keys = {int(k) for k in raw_old_slots}` inside `compute_entry_config_diff`. The normalization is applied in exactly the same way. `diff.pairs_added` always contains `(str, int)` tuples, and `added_slot_nums = {slot for _, slot in diff.pairs_added}` produces the same `set[int]` as before. The `_scope_codes_to_pairs` lookup `all_codes.get(lock, {}).get(slot)` with int `slot` matches the int-keyed `all_codes` from the provider. All equivalent.

**5. `_pending_options` removal**

The old `self._pending_options` state captured `user_input` until `_persist_options_and_clear_slots` ran. The new `partial(self._clear_then_create_entry, title="", data=user_input)` captures the same dict via closure at the same point in execution. `user_input` is not mutated after the partial is created. The cancel path is actually cleaner (no leftover state).

**Conclusion:** The PR is a clean refactor. The three specific concerns (str/int slot keys, listener key types, options-flow int casts) are all handled correctly by `compute_entry_config_diff`. No regressions were found relative to the pre-PR behavior.

## Combined review findings: PR #1028

Below merges Copilot's 3 active comments (posted 2026-04-16T14:32) with the 5 internal review agents' findings. Sorted by severity.

### High confidence — both Copilot and internal agents flagged

**1. `slots_removed` docstring claims wrong key-type guarantee**

Copilot ([line 83](https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/pull/1028#discussion_r-data-py-83)) and internal agent #4 both flagged: docstring says all three slot-dict outputs "preserve the new mapping's key type", but `slots_removed` is built from `raw_old_slots.items()` so its keys follow the **old** mapping's type. Verifiably wrong.

Fix: docstring should say `slots_added` preserves new, `slots_removed` preserves old, `slots_unchanged` preserves new. Or change implementation.

**2. `EntryConfigDiff` "frozen" / "immutable" claim is misleading**

Copilot (lines [92](https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/pull/1028) + [test 145](https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/pull/1028)) and internal agent #4 flagged: `frozen=True` blocks attribute reassignment, but the contained `dict`/`set`/`list` are still mutable — `diff.slots_added[1] = ...` and `diff.slots_unchanged.add(99)` work fine. Both the docstring's "use as cached state" wording and `test_diff_is_immutable`'s name are misleading.

Fix: use `MappingProxyType` for the dicts and `frozenset` for `slots_unchanged`, OR rename the test and soften the docstring.

### Medium confidence — internal review only

**3. `slots_unchanged` key-type lookup is fragile (latent KeyError)**

Flagged by internal agents #2, #4, #5. The reconcile loop at [`__init__.py:881`](https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/blob/7d40ed6/custom_components/lock_code_manager/__init__.py#L878-L886) does `curr_slots[slot_num]` and `new_slots[slot_num]` where `slot_num` comes from `diff.slots_unchanged` (preserves *new* key type). 

In the current data flow (both `data` and `options` come from JSON storage → both str-keyed → `slots_unchanged` keys are str → both lookups succeed), it works **by accident**. Internal agent #3 confirmed no immediate regression. But if `data` and `options` ever diverge in key type — e.g. mid-flight after an options-flow write that put int-keyed voluptuous output into `data` — `curr_slots[str_key]` would `KeyError`.

The original pre-PR code used `set(curr_slots).intersection(new_slots)` which had the same fragility, so this is **not a regression** but worth hardening.

Fix: normalize `curr_slots`/`new_slots` to int keys at the top of the listener (the type annotations already claim they are `dict[int, Any]`).

### Low confidence / style — would not block

**4. Imperative loop in `_scope_codes_to_pairs`** — internal agent #1 flagged against AGENTS.md "prefer comprehensions". The grouping shape makes a clean comprehension awkward; current loop is readable.

**5. Missing Google-style `Args:`/`Returns:` sections** — internal agent #1 flagged. The new functions have prose docstrings explaining intent but no formal sections.

**6. `_clear_then_create_entry` docstring leaks caller-side guidance** — internal agents #4/#5 flagged the "Bind via `functools.partial`" wording belongs at the call site, not on the method itself.

### What's NOT a problem

- **Bug scan agent's "`partial` captures mutable `self.data`"** — `self.data` isn't mutated between the partial binding and the call in either flow path. False positive.
- **`_scope_codes_to_pairs` `lock_instances[lock]` KeyError** — agents #2 and #5 both raised this then verified it can't trigger because `_async_get_all_codes` co-populates `result` and `lock_instances`. Worth a defensive `.get()` for robustness but not a current bug.
- **Git history regression check** (agent #3) — confirmed clean refactor, no historical bugs reintroduced.

## Recommended actions

**Must-fix before merge** (Copilot will likely re-flag if not addressed):
1. Fix the `slots_removed` docstring — one-line change
2. Address the immutability mismatch — either tighten implementation (`MappingProxyType`/`frozenset`) or soften the language

**Worth folding in** (small cost, real value):
3. Normalize `curr_slots`/`new_slots` to int keys in the listener — closes the latent `KeyError` even though it's not currently triggerable

**Defer to a follow-up** (not load-bearing):
- Style items 4-6

69	def test_diff_str_keys_match_int_keys() -> None:

71

74	    flag every existing slot as "newly added" the first time the user
75	    edits options.
76	    """
77	    old = {CONF_LOCKS: ["lock.a"], CONF_SLOTS: {"1": _slot(), "2": _slot()}}

81	
82	    assert diff.slots_added == {}

84	    assert diff.pairs_added == frozenset()
85	    assert diff.pairs_removed == frozenset()
86	    assert not diff.has_changes
87	
88	
89	def test_diff_slot_dicts_preserve_new_key_type() -> None:
90	    """slots_added/unchanged use the *new* mapping's key type.
91	
92	    The listener indexes back into raw_new_slots/raw_old_slots with these
93	    keys to look up the slot config dict, so changing the key type would
94	    break those lookups.
95	    """
96	    # Both sides use str keys (typical of the listener case where both
97	    # `data` and `options` come from JSON storage round-trips)
98	    old = {CONF_SLOTS: {"1": _slot()}}
99	    new = {CONF_SLOTS: {"1": _slot("9999"), "2": _slot()}}
100	
101	    diff = compute_entry_config_diff(old, new)
102	
103	    # New mapping has str keys -> outputs preserve str
104	    assert "2" in diff.slots_added
105	    assert "1" in diff.slots_unchanged
106	    # Pair tuples normalize to int regardless
107	    assert diff.pairs_added == frozenset()  # no locks given
108	
109	
110	def test_diff_pair_added_for_new_lock_with_existing_slot() -> None:
111	    """A new lock with a slot already managed elsewhere is a NEW pair.
112	
113	    This is the key options-flow case: user has lock.a managing slot 1,
114	    then adds lock.b — (lock.b, 1) is a brand-new pair to scan, even
115	    though slot 1 is "unchanged" in the slot dict view.
116	    """
117	    old = {CONF_LOCKS: ["lock.a"], CONF_SLOTS: {1: _slot()}}
118	    new = {CONF_LOCKS: ["lock.a", "lock.b"], CONF_SLOTS: {1: _slot()}}
119	
120	    diff = compute_entry_config_diff(old, new)
121	
122	    assert diff.locks_added == ["lock.b"]
123	    assert diff.slots_added == {}
124	    # (lock.b, 1) is new even though slot 1 isn't
125	    assert diff.pairs_added == frozenset({("lock.b", 1)})
126	
127

129	    """Adding a slot creates a new pair on every existing lock."""
130	    old = {CONF_LOCKS: ["lock.a", "lock.b"], CONF_SLOTS: {1: _slot()}}
131	    new = {CONF_LOCKS: ["lock.a", "lock.b"], CONF_SLOTS: {1: _slot(), 2: _slot()}}

133	    diff = compute_entry_config_diff(old, new)
134	
135	    assert diff.slots_added == {2: _slot()}
136	    assert diff.pairs_added == frozenset({("lock.a", 2), ("lock.b", 2)})
